title: A Phone Call About Uthman's Well
script: Amir: [curious] Mom, guess what I read today. I read about the Well of Rumah and the Companion Uthman.
Mother: Ah, the Well of Rumah. I know that story well. My own father used to tell it to us.
Amir: Tell me again, I only skimmed the article quickly on my phone.
Mother: [seriously] Long ago, people in Madinah needed the good water from a privately owned well, and its owner charged very high prices.
Amir: So poor families couldn't afford clean water? That sounds really difficult for daily life.
Mother: [thoughtful] Exactly. So the Prophet asked the people, who among you will buy this well and give its water freely.
Amir: And Uthman was the one who stepped forward?
Mother: [warmly] Yes, without hesitation. He was a wealthy, generous merchant, and he first bought half of the well from its owner.
Amir: Only half at first? Why not the whole well immediately?
Mother: [explaining] The owner refused to sell the whole thing right away, so Uthman arranged to share the water on alternating days.
Amir: Did he eventually buy the rest of it?
Mother: [relieved] Yes, later he purchased the entire well, and from that day, everyone could drink freely, rich or poor.
Amir: That's such a huge gift, just quietly given to an entire city.
Mother: [reflective] The lasting part I love is that his wealth made needed water available to other people.
Amir: His charity is remembered as service given for Allah’s reward.
Mother: [carefully] Exactly, my son. The story of the well is still remembered today.
Amir: It's amazing that one act of useful charity can be remembered many years later.
Mother: [gently] That's the real lesson, Amir. Quiet generosity can outlive the person who gave it, by a very long time.

quiz.question: What was special about the well before Uthman bought it?
options: It was the only fresh water source, but expensive
It belonged to the Prophet already
quiz.explanation: There was only one well in Madinah with truly fresh, clean water, and its owner charged very high prices.

quiz.question: What did the Prophet ask the people to do?
options: Buy the well and give its water freely
Store the water for the wealthy only
quiz.explanation: The Prophet asked who among the people would buy the well and give its water freely.

quiz.question: Why did Uthman only buy half the well at first?
options: The owner refused to sell the whole well right away
He wanted to keep some money
quiz.explanation: The owner refused to sell the whole thing right away, so Uthman first bought half and shared water on alternating days.

quiz.question: What did Uthman do after buying the entire well?
options: He kept it for his family
He closed it to the public
He let everyone drink freely, rich or poor
quiz.explanation: After buying the entire well, everyone could drink freely, rich or poor.

quiz.question: What is the mother's main lesson from this story?
options: Generosity should always be publicly praised
Quiet generosity can outlive the person who gave it
quiz.explanation: The mother concludes that quiet generosity can outlive the person who gave it, by a very long time.

quiz.question: Why was the water difficult for some families?
quiz.explanation: Cost limited access to useful water.

quiz.question: What did Uthman first purchase?
quiz.explanation: The owner did not first sell all of it.

quiz.question: How did the shared arrangement work?
options: Uthman had water on alternating days
Water was available once a month
Each family bought a new well
quiz.explanation: Days were divided between the owners.

quiz.question: What happened after the whole well was purchased?
options: The water went only to rich families
quiz.explanation: The charity made the resource broadly available.

quiz.question: What makes this charity useful?
options: It meets a continuing public need
It requires an invented modern claim
quiz.explanation: Water access serves many people over time.
